mainEntity.name: Can deck stairs be built without a landing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whether deck stairs can be built without a landing depends on the total rise of the staircase and local building codes. Many codes require a landing for stairs exceeding a certain height (e.g., 12 feet of vertical rise) or for stairs that change direction. A landing provides a crucial resting point and helps break up long flights of stairs for safety and comfort. Process Clarity: We always consult local Alameda, Albany, Berkeley, and Dublin building codes to determine if a landing is required for your specific deck stair configuration to ensure compliance and safety.
acceptedAnswer.description: Building deck stairs without a landing depends on total rise and local building codes, which often require landings for taller staircases or changes in direction. Landings enhance safety and comfort.
